book_long_title: Buddha: The Awakened One, the Reinvention of Human Living
target_audience: general public, seekers, students of philosophy and history
book_summary: Gautama Buddha was one of the most wonderful things that ever happened to mankind. A prince who had everything, he walked away from it all to answer a single question — why do we suffer, and can suffering be ended? — and in answering it, he transformed the way human beings live and reinvented philosophy itself. Sheltered in a palace of pleasure, the prince saw four sights that shattered his world: an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering ascetic. He left his kingdom, his wife, and his child, and sought the truth through teachers and austerities, until near death he found the middle way. Beneath the Bodhi tree he became the Buddha, the Awakened One, and at Sarnath he set the wheel of dharma in motion, teaching the four noble truths and the eightfold path. For forty-five years he walked the roads of the Ganges plain, teaching kings and outcasts alike, and founded the sangha. At eighty he passed into parinirvana, but the teaching did not die — it spread across the world, a light that one man's inward journey had kindled for all mankind.
gist: Gautama Buddha transformed human living and reinvented philosophy by turning inward to end suffering.

chapters.name: The Sheltered Prince
chapters.chapter_summary: A prince is born to the Shakya clan, and the wise men prophesy he will be either a great king or a great sage. His father builds a palace of pleasure to shield him from suffering, but a restlessness grows in the prince, and when he rides beyond the walls he sees four sights — an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering ascetic — that shatter his world and plant the question: why do we suffer, and can suffering be ended?

chapters.name: The Great Renunciation
chapters.chapter_summary: In the dead of night the prince leaves his palace, his wife, and his child, and goes out as a seeker. He studies with the great teachers and practices severe austerities, but neither answers his question. Near death, he accepts a bowl of rice-milk and finds the middle way between indulgence and self-mortification.

chapters.name: The Awakening
chapters.chapter_summary: Beneath the Bodhi tree, the prince endures the assault of Mara and, in the deep watches of the night, sees the truth of impermanence, no-self, and the cause of suffering. As the morning star rises, he becomes the Buddha, the Awakened One, and at Sarnath sets the wheel of dharma in motion with the four noble truths and the eightfold path.

chapters.name: The Teaching
chapters.chapter_summary: For forty-five years the Buddha walks the roads of the Ganges plain, teaching kings and outcasts alike, founding the sangha, and teaching compassion, loving-kindness, and the middle way. His victory is a quiet one — over the mind's craving, aversion, and delusion — and his teaching spreads across the world.

chapters.name: The Echo
chapters.chapter_summary: At eighty, the Buddha lies down between two sal trees at Kushinagar and gives his final teaching — all compounded things are subject to decay; strive on with diligence — and passes into parinirvana. But the teaching does not die; it lives on in the sangha and in the light one man's inward journey kindled for all mankind.
